message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value / Description | Notes |
|----------|---------------------|-------|
| **Symbol** | H | |
| **Atomic number** | 1 | Lightest element |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.008 u (average) | Weighted average of isotopes |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | Highest among elements (except F) |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) | Highest of all elements |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72 kJ mol⁻¹) | Negative value indicates energy release when gaining an electron |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14 K) | Solidifies only at cryogenic temperatures |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) | Gas at room temperature |
| **Density (at 0 °C, 1 atm)** | 0.00008988 g cm⁻³ | Extremely low; lighter than air |
| **Molar volume (at STP)** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ | Standard molar volume |
| **Specific heat capacity (gas, 25 °C)** | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ | High relative to other gases |
| **Heat of formation (H₂(g))** | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) | |
| **Heat of combustion (H₂ + ½O₂ → H₂O)** | –285.83 kJ mol⁻¹ | Energy released in fuel cells |
| **Solubility in water (25 °C)** | ~1.6 g L⁻¹ | Low but significant for biological processes |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (¹H), Deuterium (²H), Tritium (³H) | ¹H is most abundant (~99.98 %) |
| **Bond dissociation energy (H–H)** | 432 kJ mol⁻¹ | Strong covalent bond |
| **Dipole moment** | 0 D (non‑polar) | H₂ is a homonuclear diatomic |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman, Balmer series | Classic hydrogen spectrum |

---

### Chemical Behavior

| Feature | Details |
|---------|---------|
| **Molecular form** | Diatomic (H₂) under normal conditions |
| **Flammability** | Highly flammable; reacts with oxygen to form water (combustion) |
| **Reducing agent** | Strong reducing agent; reduces metal oxides to metals |
| **Hydride formation** | Forms ionic hydrides with alkali/alkaline earth metals (e.g., NaH, CaH₂) and covalent hydrides with transition metals |
| **Acidity/Basicity** | In aqueous solution, H⁺ behaves as a strong acid; H₂O acts as a weak base |
| **Hydrogen bonding** | H atoms can participate in hydrogen bonds when bonded to electronegative atoms (e.g., in water, alcohols) |
| **Reactivity with halogens** | Forms hydrogen halides (HF, HCl, HBr, HI) via radical chain reactions |
| **Electrochemical potential** | Standard electrode potential for H⁺/H₂ couple is 0 V (by convention) |
| **Catalytic role** | Catalyzes many reactions (e.g., hydrogenation, hydrocracking) |

---

### Practical Uses

| Application | Role of Hydrogen |
|-------------|------------------|
| **Fuel cells** | Electrochemical conversion of H₂ to electricity (produces water) |
| **Rocket propellant** | Liquid hydrogen + liquid oxygen gives high specific impulse |
| **Ammonia synthesis (Haber process)** | Reduces nitrogen to ammonia (NH₃) |
| **Petroleum refining** | Hydrogenation of unsaturated hydrocarbons |
| **Chemical industry** | Production of methanol, ammonia, hydrogen peroxide, etc. |
| **Metallurgy** | Reduction of metal ores, purification of metals |
| **Food industry** | Hydrogenation of fats and oils |
| **Medical imaging** | Deuterated water (D₂O) used in NMR spectroscopy |

---

### Safety & Handling

- **Explosive limits**: 4 %–75 % H₂ in air (lower explosive limit 4 %, upper 75 %)
- **Ventilation**: Must be well‑ventilated to avoid accumulation
- **Cryogenic hazards**: Liquid hydrogen is extremely cold (−253 °C); causes frostbite and material embrittlement
- **Tritium**: Radioactive isotope; requires special handling and containment

---

#### Quick Reference

- **Atomic number**: 1
- **Symbol**: H
- **Boiling point**: –252.9 °C
- **Melting point**: –259.2 °C
- **Density**: 0.0000899 g cm⁻³
- **Ionization energy**: 13.6 eV
- **Electronegativity**: 2.20
- **Isotopes**: ¹H (protium), ²H (deuterium), ³H (tritium)

These properties make hydrogen unique among elements: it is the lightest, most abundant, and highly reactive, yet it is also a clean energy carrier when used in fuel cells or combustion.
